header: IN THE LAHORE HIGH COURT, LAHORE
Order with signatures of Judge, and that of parties or counsel,
10.11.2026 Ch. Muhammad Tariq Javed, Advocate for the petitioner.
Miss. Rashida Parveen, Assistant District Public
body: M/S Mian Pervaz Hussain & Omais Nasir Bhatti, Advocates for the complainant.

Haseeb (petitioner), through instant petition, seeks post-arrest bail in case FIR No.391, dated 08.09.2025, for offences under Sections 302 & 34 PPC, registered at Police Station Kaleki Mandi, District Hafizabad.

3. The prosecution case, briefly stated, as reflected from the record, is that on 07.09.2025, at about 11:30 p.m., the complainant, injured Nazar Abbas and other witnesses were present at the cattle shed. In the meanwhile, the petitioner, Haseeb, armed with a Sota and a hatchet, accompanied by two unknown accused, arrived at the spot and raised a lalkara to teach Nazar Abbas a lesson for having exchanged hot words with him. Thereafter, the petitioner inflicted successive Sota blows on the person of Nazar Abbas, which landed on different parts of his body. Afterwards, he discarded the said weapon and delivered a hatchet blow, which allegedly caused injuries on his neck and left ear. As a result of it, Nazar Abbas Crl. Misc. No.57482-B/26 2 succumbed to injuries at the spot. The instant petition has been filed on the ground of statutory delay in the conclusion of the trial, and the learned counsel has not discussed merits of the case.

4. The petitioner, at the time of his arrest, i.e. 10.09.2025, was juvenile, and after the submission of the report under Section 173 Cr.P.C., the charge was framed on 12.03.2026, i.e., after a lapse of more than six months approximately. The claim of the present petitioner of being under the age of 18 years was subsequently confirmed vide order dated 12.08.2026, wherein the petitioner’s age was declared as 17-years; the same is not disputed by the complainant side. As far as the argument advanced by learned counsel for complainant that the statutory period be considered from the date of declaration of juvenility of the petitioner is concerned, it is of no force, for the reason that petitioner was already a juvenile at the time of his arrest, which was subsequently found to be correct after 11 months, whereas till the framing of charge, i.e., 12.03.2026, a period of more than six months already had elapsed and the trial of the present petitioner was not in progress; therefore, this is not a legal argument [ ].

5. The record further reveals that, in the petitioner’s case, since his arrest and after the framing of the charge, a considerable time of six months lapsed, and if the same be taken into consideration, no delay is attributed to him, and the prosecution could not give any plausible explanation to point out a single circumstance establishing that such a delay is attributed to the [ ] Mehran v. Ubaid Ullah and others (PLD 2024 SC 843) Crl. Misc. No.57482-B/26 3 petitioner, disentitling him the post arrest bail on the ground of statutory delay [ ]. Sub Section 5 of Section 6 of the Juvenile Justice System Act, 2018 reads as under:- “Where the Juvenile Court is of the opinion that the delay in the trial of a juvenile has not been occasioned by an act or omission of such juvenile or any other person acting on his behalf or in exercise of any right or privilege under any law for the time being in force, such juvenile shall be released on bail if he has been detained for a continuous period exceeding six months and whose trial has not been completed.”

From the plain reading of the above section, it is manifestly clear that a juvenile has earned a right to be released on bail on the ground of statutory delay in the conclusion of the trial after incarceration of six months, provided that the delay was not occasioned due to his act or omission. Reliance is placed on Khawar Kayani’s case [ ] wherein it has been held that the heinous nature of the offences does not bar the release of a juvenile on bail under section 6(5) of the Act. Similarly, initial duty to determine the age of an accused who appears or claims to be a juvenile lies with the police. When the police fail in this duty, it passes on to the court. Therefore, any time spent by the court in making this determination constitutes an act of the court, which cannot be construed as delay caused by the petitioner in the trial [ ].

[ ] Shakeel Shah v. The State and others (2022 SCMR 1), and Nadeem Samson v. The State and others (PLD 2022 SC 112) [ ] Khawar Kayani v. The State and others (PLD 2022 SC 551) [ ] Saleem Khan v. The State and others (PLD 2020 SC 356), Mehran v. Ubaid Ullah and others (supra)

Crl. Misc. No.57482-B/26 4 6. For what has been discussed above, this petition is accepted and the petitioner is allowed post-arrest bail, subject to his furnishing bail bonds in the sum of Rs.2,00,000/- (two lac) one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the learned trial court. Before parting with this order, I deem necessary to observe that the observations made hereinabove are tentative in nature and shall have no bearing on any of the other proceeding connected to this case [ ].
Judge Jahanzaib* Approved for reporting Judge [ ] Mudassar Altaf and another v. The State (2010 SCMR 1861)
